{{Quote|Tarkin is not a ''reasonable'' man at the ''best'' of times.|Finis Valorum|<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />}}
'''Ranulph Tarkin''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] from [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] who became an important [[Politics/Legends|political]] figure in the waning years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Born into the wealthy [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]], Ranulph spent his younger years further increasing the family's wealth and solidifying Eriadu's hegemony in the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] and the broader [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. He became determined that the Republic could not be secure without centralized armed forces and demanded the restoration of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], forming his own fleet and army, the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]], as a prototype for the new force. By [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], Tarkin was serving as the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] for the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] and was the leader of the Senate's [[Militarists/Legends|Militarist]] faction, becoming the Senate's most vocal advocate for re-armament.

When [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]] created a crisis by [[Pirate/Legends|pirating]] the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] shipments during a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] shortage, Tarkin saw his opportunity to win the day. He pressured Trade Federation [[Minister]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] into giving up the location of a secret summit on [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]] in which Tarkin's political rival Senator [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] and a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] delegation would mediate between the [[Stark Commercial Combine]] and the Trade Federation. At Gunray's signal that all parties were assembled, Tarkin sent his full paramilitary force to Troiken, determined to stamp out Stark's pirates by force of arms and prove the value of a strong military once and for all.

The attack went awry when Stark anticipated that the senator would ambush him and infected Tarkin's fleet with a [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigational computer]] virus. Tarkin was among the reduced fleet that made the jump to Troiken, where they were battered by Stark's navy. Tarkin had to abandon ship and seek shelter in the deserted mines of [[Mount Avos]] with the Jedi and Valorum. There he fell apart, dejected at his loss, and was inclined to give up. The Jedi and Tarkin's aide, [[Jace Dallin]], took over leadership of Tarkin's army and held out against Stark's troops, building a burning resentment and shame inside Tarkin. Finally, as victory neared under [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], Tarkin took his fate back in his own hands and absconded with an explosive. Sacrificing himself, he released a swarm of carnivorous [[challat eater]]s from behind a cave-in, killing himself but taking Stark's troops, trapped by Koon's strategy, with him. In the aftermath, due to the political influence of the [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]], Ranulph Tarkin's reputation remained strong and he was recalled as the "Hero of Troiken" for his part in Stark's defeat.

==Biography==
===The rise of a Militarist===
{{Quote|We see now the ''folly'' of not having a strong central Republic army and navy! The Jedi, good as they are, are not directly answerable to this chamber! How can we hope to negotiate successfully without military might? When will this chamber wake up and make the Republic Army and Navy ''official''?!|Ranulph Tarkin, addressing the Galactic Senate|<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />}}
[[File:Ranulf_Tarkin.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ranulph Tarkin, overseeing work at a QOM shipyard]]
Born in [[97 BBY]], Ranulph Tarkin was a scion of the influential [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]] of [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], which was the most powerful of Eriadu's [[Quintad/Legends|Quintad]] ruling families<ref name="Warfare" /> and exercised significant influence over [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] [[Politics/Legends|politics]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Trial">''[[Jedi Trial]]''</ref> Tarkin served in the [[Seswenna Defense Forces]], the [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] [[Planetary Security Forces|Planetary Security Force]], and in [[66 BBY/Legends|66 BBY]], he led a successful campaign against the [[Delmaasi pirates/Legends|Delmaasi pirates]]. He later became an executive at [[Quintad Orbital Manufacturing]], a Seswenna sector firm that produced military hardware, and during his tenure, Tarkin brokered a number of contracts with various military manufacturers from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], to lease them space in some of QOM's [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] and factories.<ref name="Warfare" />

By [[57 BBY/Legends|57 BBY]], Tarkin was the most influential figure in the entire Seswenna sector. However, he became concerned by the gradual decline in law and order across the Republic due to rising levels of bribery and corruption. Tarkin determined to take action against the rising lawlessness and after handing control of QOM to [[Ranulph Tarkin's cousin|one of his cousins]], he convinced [[Ulm Brashere]]&mdash;Seswenna's [[Senator/Legends|representative]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]&mdash;to persuade the Republic's leader [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Thoris Darus]] to appoint Tarkin as Seswenna's [[Governor-General/Legends|Governor-General]]. Tarkin's new position gave him command over the sector's military forces, and he set about enhancing the Seswenna Defense Force, building new [[Warship/Legends|warships]] in QOM's facilities. However, the construction effort attracted the attention of inspectors from the Republic's [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]], who shut down Tarkin's operation and searched the QOM shipyards for regulatory breaches. In frustration, Tarkin looked elsewhere to expand his forces and he struck a number of lend-lease deals with some [[Starshipwright|shipwrights]] to whom QOM had close ties, which placed dozens of [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] under Eriaduan command.<ref name="Warfare" />

Subsequently, Tarkin negotiated a number of mutual defense agreements with neighboring sectors, to merge their Planetary Security Forces in times of need and to harmonize their military operations. He then entered further arrangements with more distant sectors, to exchange navigational data and to allow the safe passage of his military forces across their territories. Tarkin's combined force became known as the "[[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Outland Regions Security Force]]" and developed in a regional military power.<ref name="Warfare" /> He viewed the armada as a prototype [[Republic Army]] and [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], convinced that if he could display military might in action, the Senate would realize the advantages of a proper military. Tarkin took personal command of the ORSF, styling himself as [[General/Legends|General]] Tarkin, wearing clothing in the cut of a military uniform and bearing rank badges, and taking the [[Republic light assault cruiser]] [[Invincible (Stark Hyperspace War)|''Invincible'']] as his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]]. His [[Aide/Legends|aide]], [[Jace Dallin]] of [[Rendili/Legends|Rendili]], also served as his military attache and second-in-command.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

===Political career===
{{Quote|A monster of our own creation. The Trade Federation didn't become powerful by exploiting the Outer Rim. It was supported by Eriadu's own House Valorum, and supported by Tagge and others.|Ranulph Tarkin, on the Trade Federation, whilst in attendance at a gala on Malastare|<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />}}
[[File:RanulphSenate.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ranulph Tarkin addresses the Senate.]]
The [[Judicial/Legends|Judicials]] were alarmed by Tarkin's militaristic ambitions and some suspected that he planned to break away from the Republic and form an empire of his own. Affronted by their mistrust, Tarkin determined to rebut the aspersions against his loyalty to the Republic by becoming the senator of the Seswenna sector in [[54 BBY/Legends|54 BBY]], and he was succeeded as Governor-General by his cousin [[Garvedon]].<ref name="Warfare" /> Following his arrival on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the Republic's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]].
Tarkin became a leading figure in the government of the Galactic Republic.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> He expressed his belief that the Planetary Security Forces were weak and would be unable to counter a serious military threat, and he became embroiled in a legal dispute with the [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]]. After attaining appointments to several important committees, Tarkin used his position to summon Judicial Department [[minister]]s before [[Holocamera/Legends|holocameras]], to publicly challenge their opposition to his bellicose stance. He also claimed that he would be willing to turn the ORSF over to the Judicial Department, but only if the security force were to be part of a wider Republic military<ref name="Warfare" />

Tarkin's aim of forging a strong Republic military found some support among other senators and Tarkin led the [[Militarists/Legends|Militarist]] faction in the Galactic Senate, in which capacity he passionately argued for the revival of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], counting the Judicial Forces and [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] insufficient to protect the Republic. Instead, he held that the Republic had need of a well-armed and centralized [[Army/Legends|army]] and [[Navy/Legends|navy]] in order to maintain true security. In this, he was opposed by a faction who thought that military might would only lead to war-mongering and abuse of power, instead preferring diplomatic solutions. Senator [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] was a frequent spokesman for this party, and served as Tarkin's leading rival in the Senate.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> Tarkin's designs also attracted support from some of the Senate's [[Reformist]] faction, who worked with him to make the Judicial Forces more effective.<ref name="Warfare" />

In 54 BBY, Tarkin attended a gala that was held in the [[Eriaduan consulate]] on the planet [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]], to congratulate the recent winners of the [[Vinta Harvest Classic/Legends|Vinta Harvest Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] event. During the festivity, Tarkin discussed the state of affairs in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] with fellow senators [[Pax Teem]] and [[Vidar Kim]], the [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]] [[Bor Gracus]], and the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] [[Vigo/Legends|vigo]] [[Cabra|Boss Cabra]]. They debated the rise to power of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], an influential [[Starship/Legends|shipping]] concern, and Tarkin claimed that the Federation had grown strong only as a result of the support that it had received from the [[Noble/Legends|noble]] families [[House Valorum/Legends|House Valorum]] and the [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]]. He also mentioned a rumor that he had heard regarding a recent deal that the [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] businessman [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask]] had brokered a deal between the Federation and the trade guilds of the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] and the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]]. The Eriaduan was introduced to the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] ambassador [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], an [[Aide/Legends|aide]] to Vidar Kim, and the young Human made a great impression on Tarkin, who enjoyed hearing Palpatine's views on the Federation.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

===Seizing an opportunity===
{{Quote|Excellent. We will destroy these pirate scum and the objections of ineffectual leaders like Valorum will be swept aside. The Republic will have a strong military&hellip;and a strong new ''leader''.|Ranulph Tarkin, to Nute Gunray|<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />}}
In [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], Tarkin saw a prime opportunity to put his forces to use. [[Pirate/Legends|Pirate]] [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]], leader of the great fleet of renegades known as the [[Stark Commercial Combine]], had been preying on the Trade Federation's shipping and selling the captured cargo cheaply on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. When the planet [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]] was struck with a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] shortage, Stark began pirating the precious healing fluid, leading the Trade Federation to threaten to cut off trade to the Rim entirely if the Senate did not allow them to increase their allotted defense complement. As he did with most issues, Tarkin took the opportunity to argue in the Senate yet again for the formation of an official army and navy, but Valorum rebutted him.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> Tarkin also threatened that if the Judicials could not resolve the situation by themselves, he would send in the Outland Regions Security Force to eliminate Stark's pirates.<ref name="Warfare" />

[[File:Dallin_Tarkin.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tarkin with his aide, Jace Dallin, on the ''Invincible''{{'s}} bridge]]
Instead of a military solution, Valorum negotiated a secret summit between Stark and the Trade Federation at an undisclosed location, where the Senator and a Jedi delegation would be present as mediators. Tarkin was of the belief that force, not negotiation, was the best way to eliminate Stark as a threat. To that end, he spoke secretly with [[Minister]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], a senior Trade Federation official who would represent the Trade Federation at the summit. Tarkin struck a deal with Gunray to lead Tarkin's forces to the summit, where he could kill Stark and destroy his gathered forces. The senator believed that such an attack would not only end the threat of the Stark Combine, but also convince the Senate to make his fleet and troops the official navy and army and vault him to the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor's]] office as a hero. Gunray nearly backed out over worries that they would be too easily exposed, but knowing that the Trade Federation had conspired with [[Xucphra Corporation]] to manufacture the bacta shortage, Tarkin blackmailed Gunray into giving up the conference's location&mdash;[[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]].<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

Tarkin had Dallin ready his troops, and the Outland Regions Security Force was recast as the "Republic Navy" and "Republic Army" as a deliberate propaganda statement.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /><ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Sympathetic elements within the Judicial Forces also lent Tarkin several [[Battalion/Legends|battalions]] of [[Special Tactics trooper|special-missions assault troops]], to provide the ORSF with a ground assault force for the duration of the operation.<ref name="Warfare" /> Commanding from his flagship ''Invincible'', Tarkin eagerly awaited Gunray's signal that Stark was present at the conference site. Tarkin harbored some thoughts of simply [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombarding]] the conference site when he arrived, eliminating not only Stark but also his rival Valorum and Gunray, who could implicate him in the scheme. He never got the chance to follow through on those ruminations, as when he had to fleet jump into hyperspace on receipt of Gunray's signal, the ships' [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computers]] were scrambled. Stark had learned of Tarkin's fleet and used Gunray's own transmission to infect the ships' navicomputers<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> with a [[Tionese program]], a type of [[Computer/Legends|computer]] virus.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

===A real war===
{{Quote|Might as well give Stark what he wants&mdash;he's going to get it anyway. We gave it our best shot and we&hellip;missed.|Ranulph Tarkin|<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />}}
[[File:RanulphTarkinActionHero.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Tarkin strides across the battlefield toward safety.]]
Tarkin's ''Invincible'' was one of only a handful of ships which made the jump correctly to Troiken; the others were scattered across the galaxy and many destroyed. Over Troiken, Tarkin found himself badly outnumbered by Stark's fleet. With only a third of his forces, Tarkin could not outfight Stark's flotilla, and the ''Invincible'' came under heavy attack. Horror-struck at this reversal from his glorious plans, Tarkin was indecisive on the bridge. Valorum contacted him from the surface, where he and the Jedi had escaped Stark's conference room ambush with Gunray in tow, and relayed instructions to have his fleet land on the [[Lycinder Plain]] at the foot of the [[Hormick Range]]. There, in the abandoned [[Spice/Legends|spice]] mines within [[Mount Avos]], they would have a defensible position against the Stark Combine's soldiers. Tarkin instinctively recoiled against taking orders from Valorum, but with ''Invincible'' nearly destroyed he was forced to accept the plan. He had Dallin relay the evacuation orders which sent all personnel to [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]]. He then took a [[Escape pod/Legends|life-pod]] to the surface with Dallin, as his own shuttle had been destroyed.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

Landing on the plain, Tarkin and Dallin struggled to the mountain under fire. Tarkin immediately regretted leaving ''Invincible'' for this battlefield, but he was harboring only illusions of security, as the flagship's plummeting wreckage showed. They reached the caves, where inadequate supplies made hopes of holding out more than a week slim. Dejected at the failure of his plan, Tarkin was inclined to simply surrender. In the caves, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] took over the leadership role from his Master [[Tyvokka/Legends|Tyvokka]], a [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Councilor]] who had died after sustaining injuries in the conference room. Councilor [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] and Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] were also present. Koon's telepathic powers allowed him to read Stark's mind from afar, and learn that a major ground assault was on the way. Tarkin's soldiers successfully defended Mount Avos under Jedi leadership, through a series of desperate engagements. Tarkin resented the fact that the Jedi had usurped his command role. Stuck as a spectator, Tarkin maintained that they should surrender, disbelieving that the Jedi would find success.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

When the Jedi devised a plan to sneak Valorum and Gunray offworld to let the Senate know that they had survived and convince the Republic to send support, Koon offered to evacuate Tarkin as well. Tarkin was enraged, seeing this as an attempt to pack him off so that his command could be even more thoroughly stolen from him. He insisted on staying behind. Gallia was able to escape with the politicians, while Jinn and his apprentice [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] returned from the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] with Jedi Master [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] and his apprentice [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] in tow; they had arrived after fleeing Thyferra with evidence that the bacta shortage had been faked. When Vos and Kenobi disturbed a nest of [[challat eater]]s, the Jedi had to collapse a tunnel to trap the carnivorous insect swarms.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

===The Hero of Troiken===
{{Quote|You ''stole'' my command from me. Stole the ''glory'' meant for me. Now I take it ''back''. I will ''complete'' my mission and my name will be remembered by all as the man who ''destroyed'' the Stark Collective.|Ranulph Tarkin, to Plo Koon|<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />}}
[[File:RanulphExtraCrispy.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tarkin's body, in the immediate wake of the blast releasing the challat eaters]]
When word came that the Senate had decided against sending relief to Troiken, Tarkin was more convinced than ever that they could not win. Koon summoned the Jedi together in a plan, once more cutting Tarkin out of the leadership. Koon used his telepathy to convince Stark, whose coalition was crumbling, to defect and provide the patch for the navicomputer virus which had swept the Republic, which was broadcast to Coruscant. A Jedi starfighter force, transported by Trade Federation ships, jumped to Troiken and engaged the combine. Meanwhile, as Stark's forces charged into Mount Avos, the Republic forces fled out rear exits, which they planned to block behind them with explosive charges, trapping Stark's men. Though Koon's plan could lead to victory on its own, Tarkin saw his last chance to contribute to the war effort and be a hero. He stole the explosive charge for the final exit and proceeded into the tunnels. Koon attempted to reason with him telepathically, but Tarkin set off the charge to clear the cave-in which had blocked off the challat eaters, killing himself in the process. He received his final wish, becoming the man who utterly destroyed the Stark Combine, when the challat eaters consumed Stark's trapped soldiers.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

The remnants of Stark's forces surrendered, and the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] was over; so too was Tarkin's fleet. His opponent, Valorum, was made a hero in the aftermath. Tarkin's own family struck a political bargain with him, supporting Valorum's [[Supreme Chancellor election, 40 BBY|election]] as Supreme Chancellor in [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]] in exchange for securing Tarkin's reputation as a war hero himself.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> Valorum's lauding of the deceased senator as the "Hero of Troiken," a pivotal figure and expert leader who played a vital role in winning the Stark Hyperspace War, and posthumous decoration of Tarkin increased support for Militarism in the Senate.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> His position as senator was eventually filled by a relative, [[Shayla Paige-Tarkin]].<ref name="Jedi Trial" /> Tarkin's dream of a Republic military was granted in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] with the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]], a policy of Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, a political patron of Ranulph Tarkin's younger cousin [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Damn you, Valorum! This is ''my'' command! ''Mine''! ''I'' will decide where my troops go and when!|Ranulph Tarkin, to Finis Valorum|<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />}}
Ranulph Tarkin firmly believed in militarism, supporting the re-formation of the Republic armed forces.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> He was alarmed by the breakdown in order across the [[Rim Worlds]]<ref name="Warfare" /> and he became convinced that the Galactic Republic could only be secure with a strong military. He saw force as the answer to many problems, and felt that even negotiations could not be successful without the backing of powerful armed forces. Tarkin had ambitions of becoming Supreme Chancellor, and believed that if the Senate could be made to see the advantages of a strong military in a practical demonstration, he would be swept into a leadership role. It was for that reason that he formed his private prototype military force and deployed it against the Stark Combine at Troiken. Tarkin was also a [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentrist]], preferring only Humans in his military.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

A prideful man, Tarkin found it difficult to surrender command. He had great ambitions, and when they were dashed around him on Troiken, he found the situation intolerable. He was at first disposed to give up, surrendering to Stark. As the survivors held out, Tarkin was increasingly disturbed by the fact that he had been rendered irrelevant as the Jedi and Jace Dallin stepped up to lead. He resented the others, believing they could not truly succeed. As they continued holding out, Tarkin felt that they would be robbing him of credit for a mission that he had devised, the success of which should rightfully be attributed to him. Finally, driven to near madness by frustrated ambition, Tarkin sacrificed himself to unleash the challat eaters, making himself a martyr in hopes of destroying Stark's forces himself and regaining credit for victory, even if posthumous. It would be better than living to be made a fool by Valorum and his allies.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

For all his militarism, Tarkin was not an effective commander in the field. He counted on simple might to see him through, feeling that he was guaranteed success. Though he styled himself a general, he froze when faced with adversity over Troiken and was reduced to parroting Dallin's orders and accepting Valorum's advice. Once on the ground, he was little better off, left a spectator as Dallin and Koon took over military command. Valorum simply considered him a "damned fool"&mdash;though his opinion was colored by political opposition.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I think we decided he was an uncle or something.|John Ostrander, on Ranulph Tarkin's relationship to Wilhuff Tarkin|<ref name="Ostrander">{{JCFCite|url=posts/7125682|board=Literature|thread=The Official John Ostrander Discussion Thread|user=[[John Ostrander|jfostrander]]|date=2002-05-30|time=10:20 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930193026/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-official-john-ostrander-discussion-thread.5863919/page-3}}</ref> <!-- board: Literature; thread: The Official John Ostrander Discussion Thread; user: jfostrander: time: May 30, 2002 at 10:20am -->}}
The character of Ranulph Tarkin was created by [[Dark Horse Comics]] writer [[John Ostrander]] for the comic arc ''[[Star Wars: The Stark Hyperspace War]]'' as one of the major figures involved in instigating the war. Artist [[Davidé Fabbri]] drew Tarkin, creating his visual appearance.<ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War" /> Tarkin was conceived of as a relative of famous [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] villain [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] Wilhuff Tarkin, but Ostrander left the relationship vague, deciding Ranulph was likely Wilhuff's uncle.<ref name="Ostrander" /> In ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', [[Daniel Wallace]] canonized Ranulph Tarkin as Wilhuff's cousin.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />
